column1: # Multipart POST rows for `/update/extract` (issue #258).
# Columns: name<TAB>status<TAB>url<TAB>part-name<TAB>input-file<TAB>mime
# `url` is core-relative like `manifest-errors.tsv` (everything after
# `/solr/`), never a bare GET (hence this file being separate from
# `manifest.tsv`, which is core-relative GETs only per CLAUDE.md) and never a
# JSON body (hence separate from `manifest-errors.tsv`, whose runner models
# JSON bodies). `input-file` names a file under `solr-ref/extract-inputs/`;
# `mime` is the declared `Content-Type` of the multipart file part, and may be
# empty (defaults to `application/octet-stream`, matching `capture.sh`'s own
# `cap_extract`/`cap_extract258` default).
# Every row's part name is `file`, matching every capture in
# `solr-ref/capture.sh`'s #171 and #258 blocks.
# `extract_html_index`/`extract_html_select` (the indexing-path captures) stay
# out of this file: they are not extractOnly responses (bare `responseHeader` /
# companion select), and the select is a two-step index→then→select flow this
# single-request runner cannot express. Issue #259 covers them in
# `tests/extract_index.rs` — the index response is matched there against
# `extract_html_index.json`, and the select's `body`/`links` value divergence
# (Wayfinder's own extraction, no fabricated `shape="rect"`) is asserted and
# documented per PRD divergence 10.
# interpretation note (stage 1, issue #258): the task spec's acceptance
# section says "all seven in-scope extract fixtures" for this file, in the
# same sentence that separately names "the corrupt-PDF 500 envelope" — read
# together, "seven" means the seven extractOnly=true SUCCESS captures, with
# extract_corrupt_pdf as an eighth, distinct case. This file includes
# extract_corrupt_pdf as an eighth row anyway: the differential harness
# is the one place that actually re-proves the 500 envelope end-to-end
# through the real multipart route (the fixture-derived unit tests only
# assert it once), and the TSV format already carries a non-200 `status`
# column for exactly this shape (see `manifest-errors.tsv`). Excluding it
# would leave the harness with no live-mode coverage of the one response this
# issue is riskiest on. Flagged for the implementor/reviewer rather than
# silently guessed.
